subject: common frog
title: Female Frogs Escape Grabbing Males by Playing Dead, 1 in 3 Do

scenes.text: Some female frogs escape a male's grip by doing nothing.
Every spring, common frogs crowd into ponds, and males grab any female they reach.
A grip can last hours. In a pile of males, a female can drown.
Scientists in Berlin filmed fifty-four grabs. Most females spun. Nearly half grunted like a male.
But one in three went stiff, legs stretched straight out. They played dead.
Nearly half broke free. Sometimes the best escape is doing nothing.

description:
When grabbed by males in the mating rush, female common frogs spin, grunt and play dead to break free.
In a 2023 Royal Society Open Science study, 83% rotated, 48% made release calls, 33% went rigid, and 25 of 54 clasped females escaped.
Which trick would you have guessed works best?
first_comment: One female lay rigid for about two minutes, then revived once the male let go. Which other animals do you know that play dead?
